children: is delivering stronger margins, but valuation remains a sticking point. Shares of the construction and power-equipment manufacturer fell 0.26% to $621.10 at 9:55 a.m. ET on November 2. DA Davidson lowered its price target to $685 from $882 while maintaining a Neutral rating, citing valuation concerns despite accelerating demand. That 22.3% cut puts the price investors pay for growth firmly in focus.

The operating numbers tell a stronger story. Caterpillar's October 29 results showed quarterly revenue of $20.7 billion, up 17%, while adjusted operating margin climbed to 20.6% from 17.5% a year earliera 3.1-percentage-point improvement. Quarterly operating cash flow reached $4.4 billion. Those figures show improving execution, although they have not prevented a more cautious brokerage assessment of valuation.

The GuruFocus snapshot adds another layer: a GF Score of 94 out of 100, with growth and momentum standing out while GF Value and financial strength score lower on the radar chart. Its displayed P/E of 24.36 keeps the earnings multiple part of the debate; a high overall score alone does not establish a bargain. The next test is whether Caterpillar can sustain margin gains and cash generation as sales rise, with power-equipment execution and construction demand both deserving attention.

title: Caterpillar Stocks Move Lower With Target Cut Putting Its Margin Premium on Trial
